detail.description:
AI-Native ops in action: from slices to self-healing networks
TM Forum Stand
Spend a focused morning on 25 June seeing AI-native operations made real-from dynamic 5G slice lifecycle management to cross-domain, self-healing fault resolution and next-gen architectures from Huawei and partners. You'll see how leading operators and vendors are collapsing MTTR, automating complexity across power, RAN and transport, and turning TM Forum blueprints into live, production-grade network automation patterns you can take home and reuse.
09:00 - 09:05 - TM Forum Blueprints for brilliance: Unleashing industry transformation
Ready to see what's next for telecom and connectivity? Join us on stage as TM Forum reveals how our Industry Missions and Open Digital Architecture (ODA) are rewriting the rules for agility, innovation, and growth for the AI-era. Discover how global leaders are collaborating to build AI-ready, cloud-native solutions that simplify operations and unlock new value; hear real-world stories of transformation from concept to cash; and learn how you can be part of the movement that's shaping the future. These sessions throughout the day are your gateway to the industry's most exciting breakthroughs.
Mark Geere, Director Product Marketing, TM Forum
09:05 - 09:25 - End-to-end 5G dynamic slice management
The 5G Dynamic Slicing Project brings industry stakeholders together to demonstrate how 5G network slices can be dynamically created, adapted, and assured to meet diverse enterprise and industry service needs. The project validates TM Forum-aligned architectures and Open APIs through real-world slicing use cases, showcasing closed-loop operations and cross-domain coordination to support interoperable, standards-based adoption and accelerate dynamic network slicing from concept to commercial deployment.
Wei He, Director of ZTE Core Network Intelligent Product Planning, ZTE
09:25 - 09:45 - End-to-End Autonomous Fault Management across multiple domains
This use case presents a comprehensive fault-management solution piloted at China Mobile that identifies and resolves base-station outages caused by failures across power/environment, wireless, and transmission domains. The solution integrates agentic single-domain autonomy and cross-domain orchestration to unify multiple domains, significantly reducing MTTR, minimizing field site visits, and improving customer experience (QoE).
Yao Yuan, China Mobile
10:05 - 10:25 - Intent based video experience operations
How Agentic AI is put into action to improve Video Experience MOS. User sets a target experience level, e.g., a desired MOS score (a numerical measure of the human-judged overall quality of an event or experience, e.g. video calls) and the system automatically determines what needs to change across radio, transport, and content-provider domains. It evaluates options, recommends the best actions, and either executes them automatically or assigns tasks to the appropriate teams. With results showing that targeted MOS scores increased by 5% in cases where close loop automation took control.
Erol Goctu, Head of Business Development/Ericsson Managed Services, Ericsson

Culture transformation

Most transformation programs don't fail on strategy or technology - they fail because change doesn't take hold in people, teams and leadership.

detail.full_title: Masterclass: Designing the brain and nerve system of autonomous networks
detail.description:
Masterclass: Designing the brain and nerve system of autonomous networks
Autonomous Networks require more than automation-they need an intelligent architecture that enables networks to sense, decide, and act with minimal human intervention. This masterclass explores the core building blocks of Level-4 Autonomous Networks, focusing on how AI-powered agents, intent-driven orchestration, and self-healing capabilities work together to create closed-loop automation across network domains.
Participants will learn how these capabilities interact across data, intelligence, and execution layers, and how operators and vendors can implement them using TM Forum frameworks, Open APIs, and modern AI architectures.
Key topics include:
Intent-driven network operations and service outcomes
AI and agent-based decision systems for network operations
Self-healing domains and closed-loop automation
The role of observability, digital twins, and knowledge graphs
Architecture patterns enabling Level-4 autonomy
This session combines visionary architecture thinking with practical implementation patterns, helping participants understand how to design the intelligence layer of next-generation networks.
Led by Olta Vangjeli, AN Programme Director, TM Forum and Dmytro Gassanov, Architect, Network and Cloud, TM Forum
Participants:

Andrey Silva, Senior Researcher, Ericsson

detail.full_title: Masterclass: The roadmap to real-world autonomous networks: From assessment to implementation
detail.description:
Masterclass: The roadmap to real-world autonomous networks: From assessment to implementation
Many operators are exploring Autonomous Networks, but the real challenge lies in moving from strategy and maturity assessment to practical deployment.
This masterclass presents a structured roadmap toward Level-4 autonomy, showing how CSPs can translate maturity assessments into concrete transformation initiatives and deploy high-value autonomous capabilities.
Through real-world examples and industry collaboration, participants will discover how to identify the most impactful automation scenarios, design scalable solution architectures, and measure business impact.
Key topics include:
Using Autonomous Network Level (ANL) assessments to define transformation priorities
Identifying and prioritizing high-value automation scenarios
Designing solution packages that combine AI, automation, and Open APIs
Measuring success through operational and business KPIs
Lessons learned from CSP deployments and industry collaboration
The session provides a practical framework for turning autonomy ambitions into deployable solutions, helping organizations accelerate their journey toward Level-4 Autonomous Networks.
Led by Olta Vangjeli, AN Programme Director, TM Forum and Dmytro Gassanov, Architect, Network and Cloud, TM Forum
